---
title: "Raw Milk Survey Analysis - 04: Outcome 3, At-Home Thermal Treatment"
output: html_document
---

Secondary outcome: predictors of at-home thermal treatment of raw milk (Q2),
among raw milk consumers only.

Run `01_data_cleaning.Rmd` first so `cleaned_survey_data.csv` exists in the
working directory.

Two samples:

- **Model T_Any** — all raw milk consumers (n = 164: 58 exclusive + 106 mixed)
- **Model T_Exclusive** — exclusive raw milk consumers only (n = 58)

Analytic sequence: the five-level heating response is tested first (Fisher's
exact with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 11 predictors), then the
outcome is dichotomized at "more than half the time", screened univariably at
p < 0.10, and carried into forward stepwise AIC selection. Finally the
dichotomization is varied to check robustness.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(gt)
library(pROC)
library(ResourceSelection)

survey_grouped <- read_csv("cleaned_survey_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Sample construction

`lv` fixes the category order for every predictor; the FIRST level is the
reference. Defining all recodes and levels in one place is what keeps this file
consistent with 02 and 03.

Note the thermal analysis uses its own information-source grouping
(`info_source_grouped`), which folds "Healer, chiropractor, naturopath" and
"Other [specify]" into a single "Other" category because of small cell counts.

```{r samples}
lv <- list(
  age_grouped            = c("18–24", "25–34", "35–44", "45–54", "55+"),
  sex_at_birth           = c("Female", "Male"),
  region                 = c("Midwest", "Northeast", "South", "West"),
  education_grouped      = c("High school or less", "Some college or technical",
                             "College graduate", "Graduate or professional"),
  politics_grouped       = c("Democrat", "Independent/Other", "Republican"),
  household_risk_group   = c("Not cohabiting", "Cohabiting"),
  taste_grouped          = c("Equal", "Pasteurized better", "Raw better", "Uncertain/Missing"),
  nutrition_belief_group = c("Equal", "Pasteurized better", "Raw better", "Uncertain/Missing"),
  raw_milk_sickness      = c("Equal risk", "Pasteurized milk", "Raw milk", "Uncertain/Missing"),
  milk_safety_concern    = c("No", "Yes, if consuming raw milk",
                             "Yes, if consuming pasteurized milk",
                             "Yes, if consuming either raw or pasteurized milk",
                             "Uncertain/Missing"),
  info_source_grouped    = c("Doctors or nurses", "Farmers", "Friends or family",
                             "Government officials", "Professors or researchers",
                             "Social media influencers", "Other")
)

survey_with_groups <- survey_grouped %>%
  mutate(
    taste_grouped = case_when(
      raw_milk_taste == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_taste == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_taste == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE                                      ~ "Uncertain/Missing"),
    nutrition_belief_group = case_when(
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Raw is better"         ~ "Raw better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "Pasteurized is better" ~ "Pasteurized better",
      raw_milk_nutrition == "They are equal"        ~ "Equal",
      TRUE                                          ~ "Uncertain/Missing"),
    raw_milk_sickness = case_when(
      raw_milk_sickness == "They are equal"                    ~ "Equal risk",
      raw_milk_sickness %in% c("Raw milk", "Pasteurized milk") ~ as.character(raw_milk_sickness),
      TRUE                                                     ~ "Uncertain/Missing"),
    milk_safety_concern = if_else(
      milk_safety_concern %in% lv$milk_safety_concern[1:4],
      as.character(milk_safety_concern), "Uncertain/Missing",
      missing = "Uncertain/Missing"),
    info_source_grouped = case_when(
      info_source %in% lv$info_source_grouped[1:6] ~ as.character(info_source),
      info_source %in% c("Healer, chiropractor, naturopath", "Other [specify]") ~ "Other",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    # Respondents who declined Q4 join the reference group, matching 02 and 03
    household_risk_group = if_else(household_risk_group == "Has at-risk member",
                                   "Cohabiting", "Not cohabiting",
                                   missing = "Not cohabiting")
  )

for (v in names(lv)) {
  survey_with_groups[[v]] <- factor(survey_with_groups[[v]], levels = lv[[v]])
}

data_T_Ronly <- survey_with_groups %>%
  filter(milk_consumed == "Raw dairy milk", !is.na(heating_binary))

data_T_RRP <- survey_with_groups %>%
  filter(milk_consumed %in% c("Raw dairy milk", "Both raw and pasteurized dairy milk"),
         !is.na(heating_binary))

predictors_T <- names(lv)

cat("T_Any sample (all raw consumers):   ", nrow(data_T_RRP), "\n")
cat("T_Exclusive sample (exclusive only):", nrow(data_T_Ronly), "\n")
```

## 2. Descriptive statistics

```{r descriptives}
summarise_cohort <- function(df, label) {
  df %>% summarise(
    Cohort          = label,
    Total_N         = n(),
    Missing_Heating = sum(is.na(heating_binary)),
    Analyzed_n      = sum(!is.na(heating_binary)),
    Heated_n        = sum(heating_binary == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Heated_Percent  = Heated_n / Analyzed_n * 100)
}

bind_rows(
  summarise_cohort(filter(survey_with_groups, milk_consumed == "Raw dairy milk"),
                   "Exclusive raw milk consumers"),
  summarise_cohort(filter(survey_with_groups,
                          milk_consumed == "Both raw and pasteurized dairy milk"),
                   "Mixed consumers (raw + pasteurized)")
) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Consistent Thermal Treatment by Consumption Group",
             subtitle = "Heats more than half the time or always") %>%
  cols_label(Cohort = "Consumption group", Total_N = "Total N",
             Missing_Heating = "Missing", Analyzed_n = "Analyzed n",
             Heated_n = "Heats consistently", Heated_Percent = "%") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = Heated_Percent, decimals = 1)
```

Does heating behaviour differ between the two consumption groups? Tested on the
full five-level response, and on never-heating specifically.

```{r group-comparison}
heat_levels <- c("Never", "Less than half the time", "Approximately half the time",
                 "More than half the time", "Always")

grp <- data_T_RRP %>%
  mutate(Group = if_else(milk_consumed == "Raw dairy milk", "Exclusive", "Mixed"),
         raw_milk_heating = factor(raw_milk_heating, levels = heat_levels)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(raw_milk_heating))

cat("Five-level heating distribution by consumption group:\n")
print(table(grp$Group, grp$raw_milk_heating))

set.seed(2026)
cat("\nFisher's exact (5-level) p =",
    round(fisher.test(table(grp$Group, grp$raw_milk_heating),
                      simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)$p.value, 4), "\n")

never_tab <- table(grp$Group, grp$raw_milk_heating == "Never")
cat("\nNever-heating by group:\n"); print(never_tab)
cat("Fisher's exact (never vs. any heating) p =",
    round(fisher.test(never_tab)$p.value, 4), "\n")
```

```{r prevalence-bar, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
ggplot(grp, aes(x = Group, fill = factor(heating_binary,
                                         labels = c("Heats half the time or less",
                                                    "Heats consistently")))) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.6, color = "white") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#d7191c", "#2b83ba")) +
  labs(title = "Consistent Thermal Treatment by Consumption Group",
       x = NULL, y = "Percentage of respondents", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## 3. Ordinal analysis: five-level heating response

Tested before any dichotomization. Seeding inside `fisher_p()` means the same
variable and data always return the same p-value, so this table and the
crosstabs below agree exactly.

```{r ordinal-fisher}
fisher_p <- function(x, y) {
  set.seed(2026)
  fisher.test(table(x, y), simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 10000)$p.value
}

prep <- function(df, v) {
  df %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), raw_milk_heating %in% heat_levels) %>%
    mutate(raw_milk_heating = factor(raw_milk_heating, levels = heat_levels)) %>%
    droplevels()
}

ordinal_fisher <- function(df, label) {
  lapply(predictors_T, function(v) {
    d <- prep(df, v)
    data.frame(Sample = label, Predictor = v, p = fisher_p(d[[v]], d$raw_milk_heating))
  }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    mutate(p_BH = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
    arrange(p)
}

bind_rows(ordinal_fisher(data_T_RRP,   "All raw milk consumers"),
          ordinal_fisher(data_T_Ronly, "Exclusive raw milk consumers")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(p, p_BH), ~ sprintf("%.3f", .x))) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Sample") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Association Between Predictors and Heating Frequency",
             subtitle = "Five-level response; BH correction across 11 predictors per sample") %>%
  cols_label(p = "Fisher's exact p", p_BH = "BH-adjusted p")
```

### Supplementary crosstabs

```{r crosstabs}
pred_labels <- c(
  age_grouped            = "Age Group",
  sex_at_birth           = "Sex at Birth",
  region                 = "Geographic Region",
  education_grouped      = "Education Level",
  politics_grouped       = "Political Orientation",
  household_risk_group   = "Cohabitation with a High-Risk Raw Milk Consumer",
  taste_grouped          = "Perceived Taste",
  nutrition_belief_group = "Nutrition Beliefs",
  raw_milk_sickness      = "Perceived Illness Risk",
  milk_safety_concern    = "H5N1 Safety Concern",
  info_source_grouped    = "Trusted Information Source"
)

build_xtab <- function(df, title) {
  lapply(predictors_T, function(v) {
    d <- prep(df, v)
    p <- fisher_p(d[[v]], d$raw_milk_heating)
    d %>%
      count(Level = .data[[v]], raw_milk_heating, .drop = FALSE) %>%
      group_by(Level) %>%
      mutate(N = sum(n),
             cell = ifelse(N == 0, "—", sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / N))) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      select(Level, N, raw_milk_heating, cell) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = raw_milk_heating, values_from = cell) %>%
      mutate(Level = as.character(Level),
             Variable = paste0(pred_labels[[v]], " (p = ", sprintf("%.3f", p), ")"),
             .before = 1)
  }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "Variable") %>%
    tab_header(title = title,
               subtitle = "Row percentages across heating frequency categories") %>%
    cols_label(Level = "", N = "n") %>%
    tab_options(table.font.size = "11px", row_group.background.color = "#F9F9F9",
                data_row.padding = px(3)) %>%
    tab_source_note(paste(
      "P-values from Fisher's exact test with Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 replicates),",
      "uncorrected for multiple comparisons; see the ordinal table for",
      "Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted values.",
      "Reference categories are listed first within each variable."))
}

build_xtab(data_T_RRP,   "Heating Frequency by Predictor: All Raw Milk Consumers")
build_xtab(data_T_Ronly, "Heating Frequency by Predictor: Exclusive Raw Milk Consumers")
```

### Supplementary heatmaps

Same content as the crosstabs above, shaded by row percentage. The fill scale is
fixed at 0-50% so shading means the same thing in both figures and across
variables; a count-based scale would mostly show which categories are large.

```{r heatmaps, fig.width=14, fig.height=13}
# Shorten the long H5N1 labels so rows don't crowd the plot
short_lvl <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming either raw or pasteurized milk", "Yes, raw or pasteurized", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming pasteurized milk", "Yes, pasteurized only", x, fixed = TRUE)
  x <- gsub("Yes, if consuming raw milk",         "Yes, raw only",         x, fixed = TRUE)
  x
}

build_heat <- function(df, title, subtitle, outfile) {
  dat <- lapply(predictors_T, function(v) {
    d <- prep(df, v)
    p <- fisher_p(d[[v]], d$raw_milk_heating)
    d %>%
      count(Level = .data[[v]], raw_milk_heating, .drop = FALSE) %>%
      group_by(Level) %>%
      mutate(N = sum(n), pct = 100 * n / N) %>%
      ungroup() %>%
      mutate(Variable  = sprintf("%s\n(p = %.3f)", pred_labels[[v]], p),
             var_order = match(v, predictors_T),
             lvl_order = as.integer(factor(Level, levels = levels(d[[v]]))))
  }) %>% bind_rows()

  dat <- dat %>%
    mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = unique(Variable[order(var_order)])),
           Label    = sprintf("%s (n = %d)", short_lvl(as.character(Level)), N))

  lvl_levels <- dat %>%
    distinct(Variable, Label, var_order, lvl_order) %>%
    arrange(desc(var_order), desc(lvl_order)) %>%
    pull(Label)
  dat$Label <- factor(dat$Label, levels = unique(lvl_levels))

  gg <- ggplot(dat, aes(x = raw_milk_heating, y = Label, fill = pct)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", n, pct), color = pct > 30),
              size = 3.6, family = "Times New Roman") +
    facet_grid(Variable ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#08519C", limits = c(0, 50),
                        oob = scales::squish, name = "% of row") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey20"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) str_wrap(x, 12), position = "top") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13, base_family = "Times New Roman") +
    theme(
      strip.placement   = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "bold", hjust = 1,
                                       size = 11, lineheight = 0.9),
      panel.grid        = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing     = unit(0.35, "lines"),
      axis.text.x.top   = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y       = element_text(size = 10.5),
      plot.title        = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0),
      plot.subtitle     = element_text(size = 11, color = "grey30", hjust = 0),
      legend.position   = "bottom",
      legend.key.width  = unit(1.6, "cm"),
      legend.text       = element_text(size = 10),
      legend.title      = element_text(size = 11))

  ggsave(outfile, gg, width = 14, height = 13, dpi = 300)
  gg
}

print(build_heat(data_T_RRP,
  paste0("Heating Frequency by Predictor: All Raw Milk Consumers (n = ", nrow(data_T_RRP), ")"),
  "Cell values are n (row %); shading reflects row percentage",
  "Heatmap_Heating_AllRaw.png"))

print(build_heat(data_T_Ronly,
  paste0("Heating Frequency by Predictor: Exclusive Raw Milk Consumers (n = ", nrow(data_T_Ronly), ")"),
  "Cell values are n (row %); shading reflects row percentage",
  "Heatmap_Heating_Exclusive.png"))
```

## 4. Univariable screening on the dichotomized outcome

`heating_binary` is 1 for "more than half the time" or "always". That threshold
was chosen because infrequent heating still means regular consumption of
unheated raw milk.

```{r screening}
screen_uv <- function(df, label) {
  lapply(predictors_T, function(v) {
    d <- df %>% filter(!is.na(heating_binary), !is.na(.data[[v]])) %>% droplevels()
    if (length(unique(d[[v]])) < 2) return(data.frame(Sample = label, Predictor = v,
                                                      n = nrow(d), min_p = NA_real_))
    m <- glm(as.formula(paste("heating_binary ~", v)), data = d, family = binomial)
    data.frame(Sample = label, Predictor = v, n = length(m$y),
               min_p = min(tidy(m)$p.value[-1], na.rm = TRUE))
  }) %>%
    bind_rows() %>%
    mutate(carry_forward = !is.na(min_p) & min_p < 0.10) %>%
    arrange(min_p)
}

screen_comb <- screen_uv(data_T_RRP,   "T_Any (all raw consumers)")
screen_excl <- screen_uv(data_T_Ronly, "T_Exclusive (exclusive consumers)")

bind_rows(screen_comb, screen_excl) %>%
  mutate(min_p = sprintf("%.4f", min_p),
         carry_forward = ifelse(carry_forward, "Yes", "No")) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Sample") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Univariable Screening on the Dichotomized Outcome",
             subtitle = "Predictors with p < 0.10 are carried forward") %>%
  cols_label(min_p = "Smallest p", carry_forward = "Carried forward")

comb_survivors <- screen_comb$Predictor[screen_comb$carry_forward]
excl_survivors <- screen_excl$Predictor[screen_excl$carry_forward]
```

## 5. Forward stepwise selection

```{r stepwise}
get_aic_candidates <- function(base_formula, predictors, data) {
  base_aic <- AIC(glm(as.formula(base_formula), data = data, family = binomial))
  tab <- lapply(predictors, function(p) {
    m <- glm(as.formula(paste(base_formula, "+", p)), data = data, family = binomial)
    data.frame(Predictor = p, AIC = AIC(m))
  }) %>% bind_rows() %>% arrange(AIC)
  list(base_aic = base_aic, aic_table = tab)
}

run_stepwise <- function(df, candidates, label) {
  cat("\n########", label, "########\n")
  if (length(candidates) == 0) {
    cat("No predictors survived screening.\n")
    return(character(0))
  }
  selected <- character(0)
  step_num <- 1
  repeat {
    base_f <- paste("heating_binary ~",
                    if (length(selected) == 0) "1" else paste(selected, collapse = " + "))
    remaining <- setdiff(candidates, selected)
    if (length(remaining) == 0) break

    res <- get_aic_candidates(base_f, remaining, df)
    cat("\n=== Step", step_num, "=== base AIC:", round(res$base_aic, 2), "\n")
    print(res$aic_table)

    if (res$base_aic - res$aic_table$AIC[1] < 2) {
      cat("\nNo further improvement >= 2 AIC units. Selection complete.\n")
      break
    }
    selected <- c(selected, res$aic_table$Predictor[1])
    step_num <- step_num + 1
  }
  cat("\nSelected:", paste(selected, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  selected
}

sel_comb <- run_stepwise(data_T_RRP,   comb_survivors, "T_Any (all raw consumers)")
sel_excl <- run_stepwise(data_T_Ronly, excl_survivors, "T_Exclusive (exclusive consumers)")
```

## 6. Final models

```{r final-models}
fit_final <- function(df, selected, label) {
  if (length(selected) == 0) return(NULL)
  m <- glm(as.formula(paste("heating_binary ~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))),
           data = df, family = binomial)
  list(model = m, label = label)
}

model_T_any  <- fit_final(data_T_RRP,   sel_comb, "T_Any")
model_T_excl <- fit_final(data_T_Ronly, sel_excl, "T_Exclusive")

report_model <- function(fit) {
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
  tidy(fit$model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(Model = fit$label, n = length(fit$model$y),
           estimable = estimate < 1000 & estimate > 0.001 &
                       !is.na(conf.low) & !is.na(conf.high),
           OR_CI = ifelse(estimable,
                          sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
                          "Not estimable"),
           p_fmt = case_when(!estimable ~ "—",
                             p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
                             TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value))) %>%
    select(Model, n, term, OR_CI, p_fmt)
}

bind_rows(report_model(model_T_any), report_model(model_T_excl)) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Model") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Final Models: Consistent Thermal Treatment",
             subtitle = "Predictors selected by univariable screening and forward stepwise AIC") %>%
  cols_label(term = "Predictor", OR_CI = "OR (95% CI)", p_fmt = "p-value") %>%
  tab_source_note(paste(
    "References: High school or less, Democrat, Equal taste preference,",
    "Equal nutrition beliefs. Model n excludes respondents missing a retained predictor."))
```

```{r diagnostics}
# Hosmer-Lemeshow uses g = 5 given the small samples. A model with a single
# categorical predictor yields fewer distinct fitted probabilities than the test
# needs, in which case it returns df = 0 and the result is reported as not
# applicable rather than as a p-value.
diag_model <- function(fit) {
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
  m <- fit$model
  roc_obj <- roc(m$y, fitted(m), quiet = TRUE)
  hl <- suppressWarnings(hoslem.test(m$y, fitted(m), g = 5))
  applicable <- as.numeric(hl$parameter) > 0
  data.frame(
    Model = fit$label,
    n = length(m$y),
    Predictors = paste(attr(terms(m), "term.labels"), collapse = " + "),
    AUC = round(as.numeric(auc(roc_obj)), 3),
    HL = if (applicable)
           sprintf("X2 = %.2f, df = %d, p = %.3f",
                   as.numeric(hl$statistic), as.numeric(hl$parameter), hl$p.value)
         else "Not applicable (too few distinct fitted probabilities)"
  )
}

bind_rows(diag_model(model_T_any), diag_model(model_T_excl)) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Thermal Treatment Model Diagnostics") %>%
  cols_label(HL = "Hosmer-Lemeshow (g = 5)")
```

## 7. Sensitivity: alternative outcome definitions

The dichotomization is varied two ways: heating at least half the time, and any
heating versus never. Predictors are whatever the stepwise selected for each
sample, so this tests the finding rather than a fixed variable.

```{r sensitivity}
add_heating_defs <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    heat_primary = heating_binary,
    heat_halfin = case_when(
      raw_milk_heating %in% c("Always", "More than half the time",
                              "Approximately half the time") ~ 1,
      raw_milk_heating %in% c("Never", "Less than half the time") ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    heat_ever = case_when(
      raw_milk_heating == "Never" ~ 0,
      raw_milk_heating %in% heat_levels ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_))
}

sens_RRP   <- add_heating_defs(data_T_RRP)
sens_Ronly <- add_heating_defs(data_T_Ronly)

bind_rows(
  sens_Ronly %>% summarise(across(c(heat_primary, heat_halfin, heat_ever),
    ~ sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", sum(.x == 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(.x)),
              100 * mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>% mutate(Sample = "T_Exclusive"),
  sens_RRP %>% summarise(across(c(heat_primary, heat_halfin, heat_ever),
    ~ sprintf("%d/%d (%.1f%%)", sum(.x == 1, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(.x)),
              100 * mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>% mutate(Sample = "T_Any")
) %>%
  select(Sample, everything()) %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(title = "Prevalence Under Three Outcome Definitions",
             subtitle = "Heaters / total (%)") %>%
  cols_label(heat_primary = "Primary (> half)",
             heat_halfin  = "At least half",
             heat_ever    = "Any vs. never")
```

```{r sensitivity-models}
fit_def <- function(df, outcome, selected, sample_label, def_label) {
  if (length(selected) == 0) return(NULL)
  m <- glm(as.formula(paste(outcome, "~", paste(selected, collapse = " + "))),
           data = df, family = binomial)
  tidy(m, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
    mutate(Sample = sample_label, Definition = def_label, n = length(m$y),
           # Complete separation inflates estimates; report as not estimable
           estimable = estimate < 1000 & estimate > 0.001 &
                       !is.na(conf.low) & !is.na(conf.high),
           OR_CI = ifelse(estimable,
                          sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
                          "Not estimable"),
           p_fmt = case_when(!estimable ~ "—",
                             p.value < 0.001 ~ "<0.001",
                             TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p.value))) %>%
    select(Sample, Definition, n, term, OR_CI, p_fmt)
}

bind_rows(
  fit_def(sens_RRP,   "heat_primary", sel_comb, "T_Any",       "Primary (> half)"),
  fit_def(sens_RRP,   "heat_halfin",  sel_comb, "T_Any",       "At least half"),
  fit_def(sens_RRP,   "heat_ever",    sel_comb, "T_Any",       "Any vs. never"),
  fit_def(sens_Ronly, "heat_primary", sel_excl, "T_Exclusive", "Primary (> half)"),
  fit_def(sens_Ronly, "heat_halfin",  sel_excl, "T_Exclusive", "At least half"),
  fit_def(sens_Ronly, "heat_ever",    sel_excl, "T_Exclusive", "Any vs. never")
) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "Sample") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Sensitivity Analysis: Selected Predictors Across Outcome Definitions",
             subtitle = "Same predictors refit under each dichotomization") %>%
  cols_label(Definition = "Outcome definition", term = "Predictor",
             OR_CI = "OR (95% CI)", p_fmt = "p-value")
```
